bullets.title: GOOGL -11.5%: Search miss reignites AI monetization concerns; GCP strong but discounted
bullets.body: Search revenue grew only +12% vs. +14-15% buyside expectations as AI Mode queries drive lower monetization. Google Cloud grew +103% y/y but investors apply a lower multiple due to TPU sales (lower margin). Citi cut PT to $375 from $447 while maintaining Buy; GOOGL options showed 238% above-avg volume with P/C 0.51 ahead of earnings.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure 48% growth beats by 4pts; PT raised to $680; $25B bond sale
bullets.body: Microsoft Azure accelerated to 48% cc growth in F2Q with Q3 guide of 49-50%, 4pts above consensus. M365 Commercial grew +18%, Copilot revenue accelerated q/q, and operating margins held ~50% despite heavy AI capex. Citi raised PT to $680 from $636 (Buy); MSFT also tapped bond markets for $25B, its first issuance in 9+ years, and expects to be FCF positive in FY27.

bullets.title: DASH acquires CART for ~$17B; JPM suspends both ratings; Citi maintains DASH Buy at $255
bullets.body: DoorDash announced acquisition of Instacart at ~$65/share (26% premium), 75% cash/25% stock, with $500M+ annual synergies expected net of investments; deal expected to close end-2027/1H28. DASH 3Q showed organic GOV +23% y/y, orders +28%, adj. EBITDA $1,060M ~3% above consensus; 4Q EBITDA guide ~5% below consensus midpoint. Citi maintains Buy on DASH at $255 PT (~24x '27E EV/EBITDA); JPMorgan suspended ratings and PTs for both DASH (prior OW/$262) and CART (prior OW/$62) due to advisory conflict.

bullets.title: NOW -18%/25%: cRPO deceleration overshadows AI ACV beat; margins compress 300bps
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 subscription revenue beat by only ~$8M (thinnest in 20 quarters); organic cRPO ex-Armis decelerated to ~18.75% vs ~20% prior year. Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc (ex-Armis ~16.75%) was the sharpest step-down in disclosed series. AI NNACV +65% y/y with ACV target raised to $1.7B, but non-GAAP subscription gross margin fell 300bps YoY to 80.2% on hyperscaler/inference costs; stock fell ~17-19% after hours. Sell-side 91% buy, average PT $160.18; KeyBanc raised to $110 (UW), BMO cut to $155 (OP), Wells to $175 (OW), RBC to $165 (OP).

bullets.title: ORCL Investor Day: $225B FY30 revenue target, FCF >$30B in FY29; stock +10.7%
bullets.body: Oracle targets 34% revenue growth in FY27, accelerating to $225B+ by FY30 (35% CAGR) with operating margins >40% and EPS >$21. Crucially, only $20B incremental capital (equity+debt) needed through FY30 with FCF turning positive H2'28 and reaching >$30B in FY29 vs. prior consensus of $7.3B — cutting total funding needs from ~$60B to ~$20B. Sell-side 80% buy-rated with average PT $240.84 (66.6% upside); CRWV and NBIS cited as able to replicate similar GPU-financing/prepayment model.

bullets.title: SNDK: Hedgeye/Roth both bullish; 3Q beat, 4Q guide 10pts above Street, 40%+ CY27 growth
bullets.body: SNDK Q3 revenue beat by 6% with 4Q guidance 10 percentage points above Bloomberg consensus ($588-615M vs. $549.7M consensus); gross margins guide 54-55%, operating margins 36-37%. Roth maintains Buy at $350 PT; boot/ferri drives grew 2,585% YoY with seven MonTitan SSD controller customers expected to ramp in late-CY26. Trading at 11x 2027 P/E on >40% growth; Hedgeye flags high SBC as key negative.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: Potential merger surfaces; MRVL -11%, LITE +7.4% pre-market
bullets.body: Reports emerged of acquisition talks between Marvell Technology and Lumentum; Wolfe Research hosted a webcast on implications. MRVL fell ~11% in pre-market on dilution concerns while LITE rallied ~7.4% on takeout premium potential.

bullets.title: APP/U: Hedgeye short APP, long U; Unity Vector outperforming AppLovin post-AXON change
bullets.body: AppLovin missed its revenue guide midpoint in 2Q26 for the first time in 15 quarters; Net Revenue Per Install growth slowed to 58% from 93% and Street has cut FY28 EBITDA by 12% since 2Q. Unity Vector grew 23% sequentially vs. internal plan of 12-13%, passed $1B+ annual run rate two quarters early, and U.S. advertiser count is up 37% since early July vs. 10% for AppLovin. Both report 3Q26 next week (APP Nov 4, U Nov 5).

bullets.title: AMZN: Hedgeye/Citi both see 30%+ upside; AWS acceleration and Prime timing as key catalysts
bullets.body: Hedgeye sees 30% upside over 12-15 months with Q3 headline deceleration already priced in and AWS acceleration expected in Q4+. Buyside consensus expects 3Q AWS ~44% y/y growth vs. Street +38% and 4Q EBIT guide ~$36B vs. consensus $33B. Citi hosted a post-earnings debrief webcast with Ron Josey.

bullets.title: MNDY: JPM downgrades to Neutral on core defensibility concerns amid growth slowdown
bullets.body: JPMorgan downgraded monday.com to Neutral following its Elevate '26 conference; new Frontier service (forward-deployed engineers) and Harmony voice AI agent broaden scope but provide little defense against AI disruption debate. 20% workforce reduction from July 22 yields ~$100M annualized savings mostly reinvested; $870M buyback fully utilized with no new program planned. JPM notes early-stage product bets too premature to underwrite without evidence of core durability.

bullets.title: EQIX: Record bookings drive PT raise to $1,320; +3% on day
bullets.body: Equinox reported record bookings of $533M with RPO growing 25% y/y (4th consecutive quarter >20%) and new-deal pricing up +12%. Citi raised PT to $1,320 from $1,260, reiterating as top pick; DLR showed 330% above-average options volume ahead of its own earnings (P/C ratio 8.30), suggesting elevated put activity.

bullets.title: CVNA: +8.4% pre-market on SEC clearance; but Hedgeye flags margin and loan-book risks
bullets.body: CVNA rallied 8.4% pre-market after the SEC closed its investigation with no enforcement recommendation. However, Hedgeye is bearish: retail sales grew +39% y/y but EBIT margins are contracting with 80% of EBIT from loan monetization; CVNA underwrites 88% of loans vs. 43% for KMX, creating sustainability risk. Management stopped providing forward guidance, which Hedgeye interprets as uncertainty on loan book direction.

bullets.title: AMAT/WFE: Hedgeye removes AMAT long after 40% gain; cuts 2027-28 WFE estimates
bullets.body: Hedgeye exited its AMAT long (held since February, ~40% gain) citing crowded positioning and revised WFE estimates down $10B each year (2027: $220B, 2028: $265B vs. buyside $280-300B). Key concerns: China share losses structural, advanced packaging expectations too optimistic, HBM/memory optimizations could reduce equipment intensity per AI accelerator, and 2028 could mark a cyclical peak with potential air pocket in 2029.

bullets.title: META: FY26 capex narrowed to $135-145B; raising ~$97.5B through capital markets
bullets.body: Meta narrowed FY26 capex guidance to $135-145B and is raising approximately $97.5B through capital raises to fund AI infrastructure buildout. Hedgeye maintains META as a short in mega-cap positioning alongside GOOGL.

bullets.title: NVDA: DoJ assessing Hugging Face acquisition over AI competition concerns
bullets.body: The U.S. Department of Justice is assessing Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face over AI competition concerns. Separately, Hedgeye's signal-strength model lists NVDA among its shorts alongside META and SMCI.

bullets.title: ROKU: Q3 consensus $1.41B revenue, $0.53 EPS; reports Nov 2; options imply only ~3.1% move
bullets.body: StreetAccount consensus for ROKU Q3: revenue $1.41B (Platform $1.28B), EPS $0.53, EBITDA $163.2M at 11.6% margin. Revenue has beaten consensus 17 of past 20 quarters, EPS 16 of 20. Stock +3.8% vs S&P +0.2% since August; options imply just ~3.1% earnings move, one of the tightest in the group.

bullets.title: INTC: Q3 consensus $16.54B revenue, $0.41 EPS; options imply ~9.1% move; reports tonight
bullets.body: Intel consensus: Q3 revenue $16.54B (vs. guidance $15.8-16.8B), EPS $0.41, Data Center & AI at $6.69B. Bulls cite strong server CPU demand with six-month lead times; bears flag share loss to ARM/AMD. Revenue and EPS beat rates both 15 of past 20 quarters; options imply ~9.1% move. Buyside expects +26% y/y revenue vs. consensus +21% and Q4 gross margin expansion to 46%.

bullets.title: UBER: FTC orders personalized pricing data handover; stock at 52-week low, -32% YTD
bullets.body: The FTC ordered Uber to hand over personalized pricing data alongside eight other firms. UBER is also hitting 52-week lows, down 32% year-to-date and -0.6% on the day.

bullets.title: TMUS: +3% on ARPA upside and pricing power; postpaid ARPU guide raised to +3.5%
bullets.body: T-Mobile beat on ARPA with improved pricing power; postpaid ARPU guidance raised to +3.5% growth. The FCC separately adopted a proposal to modernize direct-to-device spectrum rules, expanding SCS bands from 5 to 13 and adding 482 MHz of spectrum — a tailwind for satellite-to-device services relevant to T/VZ/TMUS.

bullets.title: PLTR/MSFT/AAPL top Hedgeye signal-strength longs; APP/NVDA/META among shorts
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Risk Range model flags TEAM, MSFT, PLTR, AAPL as top signal-strength longs ranked by time held. Short side includes APP, SNDK (newly added), HOOD (newly added), TTD, NVDA, META, and SMCI. Recent changes: NOW, MPC, VLO exited longs; AMAT, SPCX, HOOD, SNDK, FORM entered shorts; JPM, SOFI, CVNA, LULU exited shorts.
